newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline called sharply off on bearish data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline called sharply off on bearish data.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline was called sharply lower Wednesday after weekly oil inventory data reported a large rise in gasoline supply and production.
"The APIs and the DOE's confirmed each other, so you got to believe the data," said Victor Yu, vice president with Refco Inc.

Gasoline was called 1.25 to 1.50 cents a gallon lower. Crude stocks also showed a surprising rise, and was called 35 to 40 cents lower a barrel. Heating oil was called 0.75 to 1.00 cent a gallon lower, following the oil complex.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said gasoline stocks grew a much larger-than-expected 6.51 million barrels for the May 9 week when traders had expected a build of only a one million barrels. Moreover, gasoline production rose to 8.1 million barrels per day (bpd) from 7.7 million bpd.
The Department of Energy (DOE) said in its own weekly data for the same period that gasoline stocks rose 4.7 million barrels.
Gasoline production was spurred on by a sharp rise in refinery run rates that stood at a feverish 96.9 percent versus 94.5 percent last week.
Despite the high run rates and lower imports, crude stocks grew 6.94 million barrels compared to a build expected by traders of less than one million barrels.
Distillate stocks dropped 1.10 million barrels when dealers had expected a build.
But, heating oil prices were defering to gasoline's fundamentals since distillate stocks include heating oil which is out of season while the spring and summer is when gasoline demand peaks.
Dealers expected spot crude to test key support at $20.55 which had been strong resistance before June crude's upside reversal on Monday when it rose more than $1.00 a barrel.
"We didn't rise on anything real other than short covering that day," said Rfeco's Yu, noting spot crude was in danger of giving up its new 20.50 to $21.50 range.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
